newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says PLO aided infiltrator, PLO denies.
newsitem.headline: Israel says PLO aided infiltrator, PLO denies.

text.p: Israel said on Wednesday that Palestinian police moving from the West Bank to the Gaza Strip had an "infiltrator" in their bus but the Palestine Liberation Organisation denied the report.

"An infiltrator was caught this afternoon by the army during a routine check at the Erez checkpoint (from Israel to PLO-ruled Gaza)," an Israeli army statement said. An army spokeswoman said the infiltrator was a Palestinian.

"The infiltrator was found in the trunk of the bus that was transporting Palestinian policemen from the West Bank to the Gaza Strip. The infiltrator and the bus driver were handed over to the Israeli police force (for) interrogation. The army protested to the Palestinian Authority," it said.

In Gaza, Brigadier General Ziad al-Atrash, head of Palestinian military liaison with Israel, told Reuters: "The news is inaccurate and it came after the Israeli violations of the agreement by preventing the Palestinian police from moving between Gaza and the West Bank."
Atrash said the Israeli army detained two men from the bus for only "a couple hours". He said he had received no protest from Israel.

Under interim peace deals between the Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel, the PLO rules much of Gaza and major towns in the West Bank. The areas are patrolled by PLO police. Israel occupied the West Bank and Gaza in 1967.

The PLO frequently complains Israel obstructs the movement of its officials and forces. The state of Israel geographically separates the Gaza Strip from the West Bank. In the interim deals, Israel pledged to establish a "safe passage" between the two territories but has yet to do so.
